parameters.name: allow_suspicious_udfs
parameters.description: Allows use of user-defined functions (UDFs) consisting of only one symbol xxx() without corresponding xxx_init() or xxx_deinit(). That also means that one can load any function from any library, for example exit() from libc.so

parameters.name: alter_algorithm
parameters.description: Specify the alter table algorithm

parameters.name: analyze_max_length
parameters.description: Fields which length in bytes more than this are skipped by ANALYZE TABLE PERSISTENT unless explicitly listed in the FOR COLUMNS () clause

parameters.name: analyze_sample_percentage
parameters.description: Percentage of rows from the table ANALYZE TABLE will sample to collect table statistics. Set to 0 to let MariaDB decide what percentage of rows to sample.

parameters.name: aria_block_size
parameters.description: Block size to be used for Aria index pages.

parameters.name: aria_checkpoint_interval
parameters.description: Interval between tries to do an automatic checkpoints. In seconds; 0 means 'no automatic checkpoints' which makes sense only for testing.

parameters.name: aria_checkpoint_log_activity
parameters.description: Number of bytes that the transaction log has to grow between checkpoints before a new checkpoint is written to the log.

parameters.name: aria_encrypt_tables
parameters.description: Encrypt tables (only for tables with ROW_FORMAT=PAGE (default) and not FIXED/DYNAMIC)

parameters.name: aria_force_start_after_recovery_failures
parameters.description: Number of consecutive log recovery failures after which logs will be automatically deleted to cure the problem; 0 (the default) disables the feature.

parameters.name: aria_group_commit
parameters.description: Specifies Aria group commit mode. Possible values are "none" (no group commit), "hard" (with waiting to actual commit), "soft" (no wait for commit (DANGEROUS!!!))

parameters.name: aria_group_commit_interval
parameters.description: Interval between commits in microseconds (1/1000000 sec). 0 stands for no waiting for other threads to come and do a commit in "hard" mode and no sync()/commit at all in "soft" mode.  Option has only an effect if aria_group_commit is used

parameters.name: aria_log_dir_path
parameters.description: Path to the directory where to store transactional log

parameters.name: aria_log_file_size
parameters.description: Limit for transaction log size

parameters.name: aria_log_purge_type
parameters.description: Specifies how Aria transactional log will be purged

parameters.name: aria_max_sort_file_size
parameters.description: Don't use the fast sort index method to created index if the temporary file would get bigger than this.

parameters.name: aria_page_checksum
parameters.description: Maintain page checksums (can be overridden per table with PAGE_CHECKSUM clause in CREATE TABLE)

parameters.name: aria_pagecache_age_threshold
parameters.description: This characterizes the number of hits a hot block has to be untouched until it is considered aged enough to be downgraded to a warm block. This specifies the percentage ratio of that number of hits to the total number of blocks in the page cache.

parameters.name: aria_pagecache_buffer_size
parameters.description: The size of the buffer used for index blocks for Aria tables. Increase this to get better index handling (for all reads and multiple writes) to as much as you can afford.

parameters.name: aria_pagecache_division_limit
parameters.description: The minimum percentage of warm blocks in key cache

parameters.name: aria_pagecache_file_hash_size
parameters.description: Number of hash buckets for open and changed files.  If you have a lot of Aria files open you should increase this for faster flush of changes. A good value is probably 1/10 of number of possible open Aria files.

parameters.name: aria_recover_options
parameters.description: Specifies how corrupted tables should be automatically repaired

parameters.name: aria_repair_threads
parameters.description: Number of threads to use when repairing Aria tables. The value of 1 disables parallel repair.

parameters.name: aria_sort_buffer_size
parameters.description: The buffer that is allocated when sorting the index when doing a REPAIR or when creating indexes with CREATE INDEX or ALTER TABLE.

parameters.name: aria_stats_method
parameters.description: Specifies how Aria index statistics collection code should treat NULLs

parameters.name: aria_sync_log_dir
parameters.description: Controls syncing directory after log file growth and new file creation

parameters.name: aria_used_for_temp_tables
parameters.description: Whether temporary tables should be MyISAM or Aria

parameters.name: auto_increment_increment
parameters.description: Auto-increment columns are incremented by this

parameters.name: auto_increment_offset
parameters.description: Offset added to Auto-increment columns. Used when auto-increment-increment != 1

parameters.name: autocommit
parameters.description: If set to 1, the default, all queries are committed immediately. If set to 0, they are only committed upon a COMMIT statement, or rolled back with a ROLLBACK statement. If autocommit is set to 0, and then changed to 1, all open transactions are immediately committed.

parameters.name: automatic_sp_privileges
parameters.description: Creating and dropping stored procedures alters ACLs

parameters.name: back_log
parameters.description: The number of outstanding connection requests MariaDB can have. This comes into play when the main MariaDB thread gets very many connection requests in a very short time

parameters.name: basedir
parameters.description: Path to installation directory. All paths are usually resolved relative to this

parameters.name: big_tables
parameters.description: Old variable, which if set to 1, allows large result sets by saving all temporary sets to disk, avoiding 'table full' errors. No longer needed, as the server now handles this automatically.

parameters.name: bind_address
parameters.description: IP address to bind to. Several addresses may be specified, separated by a comma (,).

parameters.name: binlog_alter_two_phase
parameters.description: When set, split ALTER at binary logging into 2 statements: START ALTER and COMMIT/ROLLBACK ALTER

parameters.name: binlog_annotate_row_events
parameters.description: Tells the master to annotate RBR events with the statement that caused these events

parameters.name: binlog_cache_size
parameters.description: The size of the transactional cache for updates to transactional engines for the binary log. If you often use transactions containing many statements, you can increase this to get more performance

parameters.name: binlog_checksum
parameters.description: Type of BINLOG_CHECKSUM_ALG. Include checksum for log events in the binary log

parameters.name: binlog_commit_wait_count
parameters.description: If non-zero, binlog write will wait at most binlog_commit_wait_usec microseconds for at least this many commits to queue up for group commit to the binlog. This can reduce I/O on the binlog and provide increased opportunity for parallel apply on the slave, but too high a value will decrease commit throughput.

parameters.name: binlog_commit_wait_usec
parameters.description: Maximum time, in microseconds, to wait for more commits to queue up for binlog group commit. Only takes effect if the value of binlog_commit_wait_count is non-zero.

parameters.name: binlog_direct_non_transactional_updates
parameters.description: Causes updates to non-transactional engines using statement format to be written directly to binary log. Before using this option make sure that there are no dependencies between transactional and non-transactional tables such as in the statement INSERT INTO t_myisam SELECT * FROM t_innodb; otherwise, slaves may diverge from the master.

parameters.name: binlog_do_db
parameters.description: Tells the primary it should log updates for the specified database, and exclude all others not explicitly mentioned.

parameters.name: binlog_expire_logs_seconds
parameters.description: If non-zero, binary logs will be purged after binlog_expire_logs_seconds seconds; It and expire_logs_days are linked, such that changes in one are converted into the other. Possible purges happen at startup and at binary log rotation.

parameters.name: binlog_file_cache_size
parameters.description: The size of file cache for the binary log

parameters.name: binlog_format
parameters.description: What form of binary logging the master will use: either ROW for row-based binary logging, STATEMENT for statement-based binary logging, or MIXED. MIXED is statement-based binary logging except for those statements where only row-based is correct: those which involve user-defined functions (i.e. UDFs) or the UUID() function; for those, row-based binary logging is automatically used.

parameters.name: binlog_gtid_index
parameters.description: Enable the creation of a GTID index for every binlog file, and the use of such index for speeding up GTID lookup in the binlog.

parameters.name: binlog_gtid_index_page_size
parameters.description: Page size to use for the binlog GTID index.

parameters.name: binlog_gtid_index_span_min
parameters.description: Control sparseness of the binlog GTID index. If set to N, at most one index record will be added for every N bytes of binlog file written, to reduce the size of the index. Normally does not need tuning.

parameters.name: binlog_ignore_db
parameters.description: Tells the primary that updates to the given database should not be logged to the binary log.

parameters.name: binlog_legacy_event_pos
parameters.description: Fill in the end_log_pos field of _all_ events in the binlog, even when doing so costs performance. Can be used in case some old application needs it for backwards compatibility. Setting this option can hurt binlog scalability.

parameters.name: binlog_optimize_thread_scheduling
parameters.description: Run fast part of group commit in a single thread, to optimize kernel thread scheduling. On by default. Disable to run each transaction in group commit in its own thread, which can be slower at very high concurrency. This option is mostly for testing one algorithm versus the other, and it should not normally be necessary to change it.

parameters.name: binlog_row_event_max_size
parameters.description: The maximum size of a row-based binary log event in bytes. Rows will be grouped into events smaller than this size if possible. The value has to be a multiple of 256.

parameters.name: binlog_row_image
parameters.description: Controls whether rows should be logged in 'FULL', 'FULL_NODUP', 'NOBLOB' or 'MINIMAL' formats. 'FULL', means that all columns in the before and after image are logged. 'FULL_NODUP', means that all columns are logged in before image, but only changed columns or all columns of inserted record are logged in after image, 'NOBLOB', means that mysqld avoids logging blob columns whenever possible (eg, blob column was not changed or is not part of primary key). 'MINIMAL', means that a PK equivalent (PK columns or full row if there is no PK in the table) is logged in the before image, and only changed columns are logged in the after image. (Default: FULL).

parameters.name: binlog_row_metadata
parameters.description: Controls whether metadata is logged using FULL , MINIMAL format and NO_LOG.FULL causes all metadata to be logged; MINIMAL means that only metadata actually required by slave is logged; NO_LOG NO metadata will be logged.Default: NO_LOG.

parameters.name: binlog_space_limit
parameters.description: Alias for max_binlog_total_size. Compatibility with Percona server.

parameters.name: binlog_stmt_cache_size
parameters.description: The size of the statement cache for updates to non-transactional engines for the binary log. If you often use statements updating a great number of rows, you can increase this to get more performance.

parameters.name: block_encryption_mode
parameters.description: Default block encryption mode for AES_ENCRYPT() and AES_DECRYPT() functions

parameters.name: bulk_insert_buffer_size
parameters.description: Size of tree cache used in bulk insert optimisation. Note that this is a limit per thread!

parameters.name: character_set_client
parameters.description: The character set for statements that arrive from the client

parameters.name: character_set_collations
parameters.description: Overrides for character set default collations

parameters.name: character_set_connection
parameters.description: The character set used for literals that do not have a character set introducer and for number-to-string conversion

parameters.name: character_set_database
parameters.description: The character set used by the default database

parameters.name: character_set_filesystem
parameters.description: The filesystem character set

parameters.name: character_set_results
parameters.description: The character set used for returning query results to the client

parameters.name: character_set_server
parameters.description: The default character set

parameters.name: character_set_system
parameters.description: The character set used by the server for storing identifiers

parameters.name: character_sets_dir
parameters.description: Directory where character sets are

parameters.name: check_constraint_checks
parameters.description: check_constraint_checks

parameters.name: collation_connection
parameters.description: The collation of the connection character set

parameters.name: collation_database
parameters.description: The collation of the database character set

parameters.name: collation_server
parameters.description: The server default collation

parameters.name: column_compression_threshold
parameters.description: Minimum column data length eligible for compression

parameters.name: column_compression_zlib_level
parameters.description: zlib compression level (1 gives best speed, 9 gives best compression)

parameters.name: column_compression_zlib_strategy
parameters.description: The strategy parameter is used to tune the compression algorithm. Use the value DEFAULT_STRATEGY for normal data, FILTERED for data produced by a filter (or predictor), HUFFMAN_ONLY to force Huffman encoding only (no string match), or RLE to limit match distances to one (run-length encoding). Filtered data consists mostly of small values with a somewhat random distribution. In this case, the compression algorithm is tuned to compress them better. The effect of FILTERED is to force more Huffman coding and less string matching; it is somewhat intermediate between DEFAULT_STRATEGY and HUFFMAN_ONLY. RLE is designed to be almost as fast as HUFFMAN_ONLY, but give better compression for PNG image data. The strategy parameter only affects the compression ratio but not the correctness of the compressed output even if it is not set appropriately. FIXED prevents the use of dynamic Huffman codes, allowing for a simpler decoder for special applications.

parameters.name: column_compression_zlib_wrap
parameters.description: Generate zlib header and trailer and compute adler32 check value. It can be used with storage engines that don't provide data integrity verification to detect data corruption.

parameters.name: completion_type
parameters.description: The transaction completion type

parameters.name: concurrent_insert
parameters.description: Use concurrent insert with MyISAM

parameters.name: connect_timeout
parameters.description: The number of seconds the mysqld server is waiting for a connect packet before responding with 'Bad handshake'

parameters.name: core_file
parameters.description: Write core on crashes

parameters.name: datadir
parameters.description: Path to the database root directory

parameters.name: deadlock_search_depth_long
parameters.description: Long search depth for the two-step deadlock detection

parameters.name: deadlock_search_depth_short
parameters.description: Short search depth for the two-step deadlock detection

parameters.name: deadlock_timeout_long
parameters.description: Long timeout for the two-step deadlock detection (in microseconds)

parameters.name: deadlock_timeout_short
parameters.description: Short timeout for the two-step deadlock detection (in microseconds)

parameters.name: default_password_lifetime
parameters.description: This defines the global password expiration policy. 0 means automatic password expiration is disabled. If the value is a positive integer N, the passwords must be changed every N days. This behavior can be overridden using the password expiration options in ALTER USER.

parameters.name: default_regex_flags
parameters.description: Default flags for the regex library

parameters.name: default_storage_engine
parameters.description: The default storage engine for new tables

parameters.name: default_tmp_storage_engine
parameters.description: The default storage engine for user-created temporary tables

parameters.name: default_week_format
parameters.description: The default week format used by WEEK() functions

parameters.name: delay_key_write
parameters.description: Specifies how MyISAM tables handles CREATE TABLE DELAY_KEY_WRITE. If set to ON, the default, any DELAY KEY WRITEs are honored. The key buffer is then flushed only when the table closes, speeding up writes. MyISAM tables should be automatically checked upon startup in this case, and --external locking should not be used, as it can lead to index corruption. If set to OFF, DELAY KEY WRITEs are ignored, while if set to ALL, all new opened tables are treated as if created with DELAY KEY WRITEs enabled.

parameters.name: delayed_insert_limit
parameters.description: After inserting delayed_insert_limit rows, the INSERT DELAYED handler will check if there are any SELECT statements pending. If so, it allows these to execute before continuing.

parameters.name: delayed_insert_timeout
parameters.description: How long a INSERT DELAYED thread should wait for INSERT statements before terminating

parameters.name: delayed_queue_size
parameters.description: What size queue (in rows) should be allocated for handling INSERT DELAYED. If the queue becomes full, any client that does INSERT DELAYED will wait until there is room in the queue again

parameters.name: disconnect_on_expired_password
parameters.description: This variable controls how the server handles clients that are not aware of the sandbox mode. If enabled, the server disconnects the client, otherwise the server puts the client in a sandbox mode.

parameters.name: div_precision_increment
parameters.description: Precision of the result of '/' operator will be increased on that value

parameters.name: encrypt_binlog
parameters.description: Encrypt binary logs (including relay logs)

parameters.name: encrypt_tmp_disk_tables
parameters.description: Encrypt temporary on-disk tables (created as part of query execution)

parameters.name: encrypt_tmp_files
parameters.description: Encrypt temporary files (created for filesort, binary log cache, etc)

parameters.name: enforce_storage_engine
parameters.description: Force the use of a storage engine for new tables

parameters.name: eq_range_index_dive_limit
parameters.description: The optimizer will use existing index statistics instead of doing index dives for equality ranges if the number of equality ranges for the index is larger than or equal to this number. If set to 0, index dives are always used.

parameters.name: event_scheduler
parameters.description: Enable the event scheduler. Possible values are ON, OFF, and DISABLED (keep the event scheduler completely deactivated, it cannot be activated run-time)

parameters.name: expensive_subquery_limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows a subquery may examine in order to be executed during optimization and used for constant optimization

parameters.name: expire_logs_days
parameters.description: If non-zero, binary logs will be purged after expire_logs_days days; It and binlog_expire_logs_seconds are linked, such that changes in one are converted into the other, presentable as a decimal value with 1/1000000 of the day precision; possible purges happen at startup and at binary log rotation

parameters.name: explicit_defaults_for_timestamp
parameters.description: This option causes CREATE TABLE to create all TIMESTAMP columns as NULL with DEFAULT NULL attribute, Without this option, TIMESTAMP columns are NOT NULL and have implicit DEFAULT clauses.

parameters.name: extra_max_connections
parameters.description: The number of connections on extra-port

parameters.name: extra_port
parameters.description: Extra port number to use for tcp connections in a one-thread-per-connection manner. 0 means don't use another port

parameters.name: flush
parameters.description: Flush MyISAM tables to disk between SQL commands

parameters.name: flush_time
parameters.description: A dedicated thread is created to flush all tables at the given interval

parameters.name: foreign_key_checks
parameters.description: If set to 1 (the default) foreign key constraints (including ON UPDATE and ON DELETE behavior) InnoDB tables are checked, while if set to 0, they are not checked. 0 is not recommended for normal use, though it can be useful in situations where you know the data is consistent, but want to reload data in a different order from that specified by parent/child relationships. Setting this variable to 1 does not retrospectively check for inconsistencies introduced while set to 0.

parameters.name: ft_boolean_syntax
parameters.description: List of operators for MATCH ... AGAINST ( ... IN BOOLEAN MODE)

parameters.name: ft_max_word_len
parameters.description: The maximum length of the word to be included in a FULLTEXT index. Note: FULLTEXT indexes must be rebuilt after changing this variable

parameters.name: ft_min_word_len
parameters.description: The minimum length of the word to be included in a FULLTEXT index. Note: FULLTEXT indexes must be rebuilt after changing this variable

parameters.name: ft_query_expansion_limit
parameters.description: Number of best matches to use for query expansion

parameters.name: ft_stopword_file
parameters.description: Use stopwords from this file instead of built-in list

parameters.name: general_log
parameters.description: Log connections and queries to a table or log file. Defaults logging to a file 'hostname'.log or a table mysql.general_logif --log-output=TABLE is used.

parameters.name: general_log_file
parameters.description: Log connections and queries to given file

parameters.name: group_concat_max_len
parameters.description: The maximum length of the result of function GROUP_CONCAT()

parameters.name: gtid_binlog_pos
parameters.description: Last GTID logged to the binary log, per replicationdomain

parameters.name: gtid_binlog_state
parameters.description: The internal GTID state of the binlog, used to keep track of all GTIDs ever logged to the binlog.

parameters.name: gtid_cleanup_batch_size
parameters.description: Normally does not need tuning. How many old rows must accumulate in the mysql.gtid_slave_pos table before a background job will be run to delete them. Can be increased to reduce number of commits if using many different engines with --gtid_pos_auto_engines, or to reduce CPU overhead if using a huge number of different gtid_domain_ids. Can be decreased to reduce number of old rows in the table.

parameters.name: gtid_current_pos
parameters.description: Current GTID position of the server. Per replication domain, this is either the last GTID replicated by a slave thread, or the GTID logged to the binary log, whichever is most recent.

parameters.name: gtid_domain_id
parameters.description: Used with global transaction ID to identify logically independent replication streams. When events can propagate through multiple parallel paths (for example multiple masters), each independent source server must use a distinct domain_id. For simple tree-shaped replication topologies, it can be left at its default, 0.

parameters.name: gtid_ignore_duplicates
parameters.description: When set, different master connections in multi-source replication are allowed to receive and process event groups with the same GTID (when using GTID mode). Only one will be applied, any others will be ignored. Within a given replication domain, just the sequence number will be used to decide whether a given GTID has been already applied; this means it is the responsibility of the user to ensure that GTID sequence numbers are strictly increasing.

parameters.name: gtid_pos_auto_engines
parameters.description: List of engines for which to automatically create a mysql.gtid_slave_pos_ENGINE table, if a transaction using that engine is replicated. This can be used to avoid introducing cross-engine transactions, if engines are used different from that used by table mysql.gtid_slave_pos

parameters.name: gtid_slave_pos
parameters.description: The list of global transaction IDs that were last replicated on the server, one for each replication domain.

parameters.name: gtid_strict_mode
parameters.description: Enforce strict seq_no ordering of events in the binary log. Slave stops with an error if it encounters an event that would cause it to generate an out-of-order binlog if executed. When ON the same server-id semisync-replicated transactions that duplicate existing ones in binlog are ignored without error and slave interruption.

parameters.name: have_compress
parameters.description: If the zlib compression library is accessible to the server, this will be set to YES, otherwise it will be NO. The COMPRESS() and UNCOMPRESS() functions will only be available if set to YES.

parameters.name: have_crypt
parameters.description: If the crypt() system call is available this variable will be set to YES, otherwise it will be set to NO. If set to NO, the ENCRYPT() function cannot be used.

parameters.name: have_dynamic_loading
parameters.description: If the server supports dynamic loading of plugins, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO.

parameters.name: have_geometry
parameters.description: If the server supports spatial data types, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO.

parameters.name: have_openssl
parameters.description: Comparing have_openssl with have_ssl will indicate whether YaSSL or openssl was used. If YaSSL, have_ssl will be YES, but have_openssl will be NO.

parameters.name: have_profiling
parameters.description: If statement profiling is available, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO. See SHOW PROFILES and SHOW PROFILE.

parameters.name: have_query_cache
parameters.description: If the server supports the query cache, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO.

parameters.name: have_rtree_keys
parameters.description: If RTREE indexes (used for spatial indexes) are available, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO.

parameters.name: have_ssl
parameters.description: If the server supports secure connections, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO. If set to DISABLED, the server was compiled with TLS support, but was not started with TLS support (see the mysqld options). See also have_openssl.

parameters.name: have_symlink
parameters.description: If symbolic link support is enabled, will be set to YES, otherwise will be set to NO. Required for the INDEX DIRECTORY and DATA DIRECTORY table options (see CREATE TABLE) and Windows symlink support. Will be set to DISABLED if the server is started with the --skip-symbolic-links option.

parameters.name: histogram_size
parameters.description: Number of bytes used for a histogram. If set to 0, no histograms are created by ANALYZE.

parameters.name: histogram_type
parameters.description: Specifies type of the histograms created by ANALYZE. Possible values are: SINGLE_PREC_HB - single precision height-balanced, DOUBLE_PREC_HB - double precision height-balanced, JSON_HB - height-balanced, stored as JSON.

parameters.name: host_cache_size
parameters.description: How many host names should be cached to avoid resolving.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.description: Server host name

parameters.name: idle_readonly_transaction_timeout
parameters.description: The number of seconds the server waits for read-only idle transaction

parameters.name: idle_transaction_timeout
parameters.description: The number of seconds the server waits for idle transaction

parameters.name: idle_write_transaction_timeout
parameters.description: The number of seconds the server waits for write idle transaction

parameters.name: ignore_builtin_innodb
parameters.description: Disable initialization of builtin InnoDB plugin

parameters.name: ignore_db_dirs
parameters.description: Specifies a directory to add to the ignore list when collecting database names from the datadir. Put a blank argument to reset the list accumulated so far.

parameters.name: in_predicate_conversion_threshold
parameters.description: The minimum number of scalar elements in the value list of IN predicate that triggers its conversion to IN subquery. Set to 0 to disable the conversion.

parameters.name: init_connect
parameters.description: Command(s) that are executed for each new connection (unless the user has SUPER privilege)

parameters.name: init_file
parameters.description: Read SQL commands from this file at startup

parameters.name: init_slave
parameters.description: Command(s) that are executed by a slave server each time the SQL thread starts

parameters.name: innodb_adaptive_flushing
parameters.description: Attempt flushing dirty pages to avoid IO bursts at checkpoints.

parameters.name: innodb_adaptive_flushing_lwm
parameters.description: Percentage of log capacity below which no adaptive flushing happens.

parameters.name: innodb_adaptive_hash_index
parameters.description: Enable InnoDB adaptive hash index (disabled by default).

parameters.name: innodb_adaptive_hash_index_parts
parameters.description: Number of InnoDB Adaptive Hash Index Partitions (default 8)

parameters.name: innodb_alter_copy_bulk
parameters.description: Allow bulk insert operation for copy alter operation

parameters.name: innodb_autoextend_increment
parameters.description: Data file autoextend increment in megabytes

parameters.name: innodb_autoinc_lock_mode
parameters.description: The AUTOINC lock modes supported by InnoDB: 0 => Old style AUTOINC locking (for backward compatibility); 1 => New style AUTOINC locking; 2 => No AUTOINC locking (unsafe for SBR)

parameters.name: innodb_buf_dump_status_frequency
parameters.description: A number between [0, 100] that tells how oftern buffer pool dump status in percentages should be printed. E.g. 10 means that buffer pool dump status is printed when every 10% of number of buffer pool pages are dumped. Default is 0 (only start and end status is printed).

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_chunk_size
parameters.description: Deprecated parameter with no effect

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_dump_at_shutdown
parameters.description: Dump the buffer pool into a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_dump_now
parameters.description: Trigger an immediate dump of the buffer pool into a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_dump_pct
parameters.description: Dump only the hottest N% of each buffer pool, defaults to 25

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_filename
parameters.description: Filename to/from which to dump/load the InnoDB buffer pool

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_in_core_dump
parameters.description: Include the buffer pool in core dump.

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_load_abort
parameters.description: Abort a currently running load of the buffer pool

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_load_at_startup
parameters.description: Load the buffer pool from a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_load_now
parameters.description: Trigger an immediate load of the buffer pool from a file named @@innodb_buffer_pool_filename

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_size
parameters.description: The size of the memory buffer InnoDB uses to cache data and indexes of its tables.

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_size_auto_min
parameters.description: Minimum innodb_buffer_pool_size for dynamic shrinking on memory pressure

parameters.name: innodb_buffer_pool_size_max
parameters.description: Maximum innodb_buffer_pool_size

parameters.name: innodb_checksum_algorithm
parameters.description: The algorithm InnoDB uses for page checksumming. Possible values are FULL_CRC32 for new files, always use CRC-32C; for old, see CRC32 below; STRICT_FULL_CRC32 for new files, always use CRC-32C; for old, see STRICT_CRC32 below; CRC32 write crc32, allow previously used algorithms to match when reading; STRICT_CRC32 write crc32, do not allow other algorithms to match when reading; New files created with full_crc32 are readable by MariaDB 10.4.3+

parameters.name: innodb_cmp_per_index_enabled
parameters.description: Enable INFORMATION_SCHEMA.innodb_cmp_per_index, may have negative impact on performance (off by default)

parameters.name: innodb_compression_algorithm
parameters.description: Compression algorithm used on page compression. One of: none, zlib, lz4, lzo, lzma, bzip2, or snappy

parameters.name: innodb_compression_default

parameters.description: Chance that we have to do a disk read to find a row or index entry from the engine cache (cache_misses/total_cache_requests).  0.0 means that everything is cached and 1.0 means that nothing is expected to be in the engine cache.

parameters.name: optimizer_extra_pruning_depth
parameters.description: If the optimizer needs to enumerate join prefix of this size or larger, then it will try aggressively prune away the search space.

parameters.name: optimizer_index_block_copy_cost
parameters.description: Cost of copying a key block from the cache to intern storage as part of an index scan.

parameters.name: optimizer_join_limit_pref_ratio
parameters.description: For queries with JOIN and ORDER BY LIMIT : make the optimizer consider a join order that allows to short-cut execution after producing #LIMIT matches if that promises N times speedup. (A conservative setting here would be is a high value, like 100 so the short-cutting plan is used if it promises a speedup of 100x or more). Short-cutting plans are inherently risky so the default is 0 which means do not consider this optimization

parameters.name: optimizer_key_compare_cost
parameters.description: Cost of checking a key against the end key condition.

parameters.name: optimizer_key_copy_cost
parameters.description: Cost of finding the next key in the engine and copying it to the SQL layer.

parameters.name: optimizer_key_lookup_cost
parameters.description: Cost for finding a key based on a key value

parameters.name: optimizer_key_next_find_cost
parameters.description: Cost of finding the next key and rowid when using filters.

parameters.name: optimizer_max_sel_arg_weight
parameters.description: The maximum weight of the SEL_ARG graph. Set to 0 for no limit

parameters.name: optimizer_max_sel_args
parameters.description: The maximum number of SEL_ARG objects created when optimizing a range. If more objects would be needed, the range will not be used by the optimizer.

parameters.name: optimizer_prune_level
parameters.description: Controls the heuristic(s) applied during query optimization to prune less-promising partial plans from the optimizer search space. Meaning: 0 - do not apply any heuristic, thus perform exhaustive search: 1 - prune plans based on cost and number of retrieved rows eq_ref: 2 - prune also if we find an eq_ref chain

parameters.name: optimizer_row_copy_cost
parameters.description: Cost of copying a row from the engine or the join cache to the SQL layer.

parameters.name: optimizer_row_lookup_cost
parameters.description: Cost of finding a row based on a rowid or a clustered key.

parameters.name: optimizer_row_next_find_cost
parameters.description: Cost of finding the next row when scanning the table.

parameters.name: optimizer_rowid_compare_cost
parameters.description: Cost of comparing two rowid's

parameters.name: optimizer_rowid_copy_cost
parameters.description: Cost of copying a rowid

parameters.name: optimizer_scan_setup_cost
parameters.description: Extra cost added to TABLE and INDEX scans to get optimizer to prefer index lookups.

parameters.name: optimizer_search_depth
parameters.description: Maximum depth of search performed by the query optimizer. Values larger than the number of relations in a query result in better query plans, but take longer to compile a query. Values smaller than the number of tables in a relation result in faster optimization, but may produce very bad query plans. If set to 0, the system will automatically pick a reasonable value.

parameters.name: optimizer_selectivity_sampling_limit
parameters.description: Controls number of record samples to check condition selectivity

parameters.name: optimizer_switch
parameters.description: Fine-tune the optimizer behavior

parameters.name: optimizer_trace
parameters.description: Controls tracing of the Optimizer: optimizer_trace=option=val[,option=val...], where option is one of {enabled} and val is one of {on, off, default}

parameters.name: optimizer_trace_max_mem_size
parameters.description: Maximum allowed size of an optimizer trace

parameters.name: optimizer_use_condition_selectivity
parameters.description: Controls selectivity of which conditions the optimizer takes into account to calculate cardinality of a partial join when it searches for the best execution plan Meaning: 1 - use selectivity of index backed range conditions to calculate the cardinality of a partial join if the last joined table is accessed by full table scan or an index scan, 2 - use selectivity of index backed range conditions to calculate the cardinality of a partial join in any case, 3 - additionally always use selectivity of range conditions that are not backed by any index to calculate the cardinality of a partial join, 4 - use histograms to calculate selectivity of range conditions that are not backed by any index to calculate the cardinality of a partial join.5 - additionally use selectivity of certain non-range predicates calculated on record samples

parameters.name: optimizer_where_cost
parameters.description: Cost of checking the row against the WHERE clause. Increasing this will have the optimizer to prefer plans with less row combinations.

parameters.name: performance_schema
parameters.description: Enable the performance schema.

parameters.name: performance_schema_accounts_size

parameters.name: performance_schema_events_statements_history_size
parameters.description: Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_STATEMENTS_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_events_transactions_history_long_size
parameters.description: Number of rows in EVENTS_TRANSACTIONS_HISTORY_LONG. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_events_waits_history_size
parameters.description: Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_WAITS_HISTORY. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_hosts_size
parameters.description: Maximum number of instrumented hosts. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_cond_classes
parameters.description: Maximum number of condition instruments.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_cond_instances
parameters.description: Maximum number of instrumented condition objects. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_digest_length
parameters.description: Maximum length considered for digest text, when stored in performance_schema tables.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_file_classes

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_file_handles

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_file_instances

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_index_stat

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_memory_classes
parameters.description: Maximum number of memory pool instruments.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_metadata_locks
parameters.description: Maximum number of metadata locks. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_mutex_classes

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_prepared_statements_instances

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_program_instances

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_rwlock_classes
parameters.description: Maximum number of rwlock instruments.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_rwlock_instances
parameters.description: Maximum number of instrumented RWLOCK objects. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_socket_classes
parameters.description: Maximum number of socket instruments.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_socket_instances
parameters.description: Maximum number of opened instrumented sockets. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_sql_text_length
parameters.description: Maximum length of displayed sql text.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_statement_stack
parameters.description: Number of rows per thread in EVENTS_STATEMENTS_CURRENT.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_table_handles
parameters.description: Maximum number of opened instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_table_instances
parameters.description: Maximum number of instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_table_lock_stat
parameters.description: Maximum number of lock statistics for instrumented tables. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated scaling.

parameters.name: performance_schema_max_thread_classes

parameters.description: Maximum number of instrumented threads. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_session_connect_attrs_size
parameters.description: Size of session attribute string buffer per thread. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: performance_schema_setup_actors_size
parameters.description: Maximum number of rows in SETUP_ACTORS.

parameters.name: performance_schema_setup_objects_size
parameters.description: Maximum number of rows in SETUP_OBJECTS.

parameters.name: performance_schema_users_size
parameters.description: Maximum number of instrumented users. Use 0 to disable, -1 for automated sizing.

parameters.name: pid_file
parameters.description: Pid file used by safe_mysqld

parameters.name: plugin_dir
parameters.description: Directory for plugins

parameters.name: plugin_maturity
parameters.description: The lowest desirable plugin maturity. Plugins less mature than that will not be installed or loaded

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Port number to use for connection or 0 to default to, my.cnf, $MYSQL_TCP_PORT, /etc/services, built-in default (3306), whatever comes first

parameters.name: preload_buffer_size
parameters.description: The size of the buffer that is allocated when preloading indexes

parameters.name: profiling
parameters.description: If set to 1 (0 is default), statement profiling will be enabled. See SHOW PROFILES and SHOW PROFILE.

parameters.name: profiling_history_size
parameters.description: Number of statements about which profiling information is maintained. If set to 0, no profiles are stored. See SHOW PROFILES.

parameters.name: progress_report_time
parameters.description: Seconds between sending progress reports to the client for time-consuming statements. Set to 0 to disable progress reporting.

parameters.name: protocol_version
parameters.description: The version of the client/server protocol used by the MariaDB server

parameters.name: proxy_protocol_networks
parameters.description: Enable proxy protocol for these source networks. The syntax is a comma separated list of IPv4 and IPv6 networks. If the network doesn't contain mask, it is considered to be a single host. "*" represents all networks and must the only directive on the line. String "localhost" represents non-TCP local connections (Unix domain socket, Windows named pipe or shared memory).

parameters.name: query_alloc_block_size
parameters.description: Allocation block size for query parsing and execution

parameters.name: query_cache_limit
parameters.description: Don't cache results that are bigger than this

parameters.name: query_cache_min_res_unit
parameters.description: The minimum size for blocks allocated by the query cache

parameters.name: query_cache_size
parameters.description: The memory allocated to store results from old queries

parameters.name: query_cache_strip_comments
parameters.description: Strip all comments from a query before storing it in the query cache

parameters.name: query_cache_type
parameters.description: OFF = Don't cache or retrieve results. ON = Cache all results except SELECT SQL_NO_CACHE ... queries. DEMAND = Cache only SELECT SQL_CACHE ... queries

parameters.name: query_cache_wlock_invalidate
parameters.description: Invalidate queries in query cache on LOCK for write

parameters.name: query_prealloc_size
parameters.description: Persistent buffer for query parsing and execution

parameters.name: range_alloc_block_size
parameters.description: Allocation block size for storing ranges during optimization

parameters.name: read_binlog_speed_limit
parameters.description: Maximum speed(KB/s) to read binlog from master (0 = no limit)

parameters.name: read_buffer_size
parameters.description: Each thread that does a sequential scan allocates a buffer of this size for each table it scans. If you do many sequential scans, you may want to increase this value

parameters.name: read_only
parameters.description: Make all non-temporary tables read-only, with the exception for replication (slave) threads and users with the 'READ ONLY ADMIN' privilege

parameters.name: read_rnd_buffer_size
parameters.description: When reading rows in sorted order after a sort, the rows are read through this buffer to avoid a disk seeks

parameters.name: redirect_url
parameters.description: URL of another server to redirect clients to. Empty string means no redirection

parameters.name: relay_log
parameters.description: The location and name to use for relay logs.

parameters.name: relay_log_basename
parameters.description: The full path of the relay log file names, excluding the extension.

parameters.name: relay_log_index
parameters.description: The location and name to use for the file that keeps a list of the last relay logs.

parameters.name: relay_log_info_file
parameters.description: The location and name of the file that remembers where the SQL replication thread is in the relay logs.

parameters.name: relay_log_purge
parameters.description: if disabled - do not purge relay logs. if enabled - purge them as soon as they are no more needed.

parameters.name: relay_log_recovery
parameters.description: Enables automatic relay log recovery right after the database startup, which means that the IO Thread starts re-fetching from the master right after the last transaction processed.

parameters.name: relay_log_space_limit
parameters.description: Maximum space to use for all relay logs

parameters.name: replicate_annotate_row_events
parameters.description: Tells the slave to write annotate rows events received from the master to its own binary log. Ignored if log_slave_updates is not set

parameters.name: replicate_do_db
parameters.description: Tell the slave to restrict replication to updates of tables whose names appear in the comma-separated list. For statement-based replication, only the default database (that is, the one selected by USE) is considered, not any explicitly mentioned tables in the query. For row-based replication, the actual names of table(s) being updated are checked.

parameters.name: replicate_do_table
parameters.description: Tells the slave to restrict replication to tables in the comma-separated list.

parameters.name: replicate_events_marked_for_skip
parameters.description: Whether the slave should replicate events that were created with @@skip_replication=1 on the master. Default REPLICATE (no events are skipped). Other values are FILTER_ON_SLAVE (events will be sent by the master but ignored by the slave) and FILTER_ON_MASTER (events marked with @@skip_replication=1 will be filtered on the master and never be sent to the slave).

parameters.name: replicate_ignore_db
parameters.description: Tell the slave to restrict replication to updates of tables whose names do not appear in the comma-separated list. For statement-based replication, only the default database (that is, the one selected by USE) is considered, not any explicitly mentioned tables in the query. For row-based replication, the actual names of table(s) being updated are checked.

parameters.name: replicate_ignore_table
parameters.description: Tells the slave thread not to replicate any statement that updates the specified table, even if any other tables might be updated by the same statement.

parameters.name: replicate_rewrite_db
parameters.description: Tells the slave to replicate binlog events into a different database than their original target on the master.Example: replicate-rewrite-db=master_db_name->slave_db_name.

parameters.name: replicate_wild_do_table
parameters.description: Tells the slave thread to restrict replication to statements where any of the updated tables match the specified database and table name patterns.

parameters.name: replicate_wild_ignore_table
parameters.description: Tells the slave thread to not replicate to the tables that match the given wildcard pattern.

parameters.name: report_host
parameters.description: Hostname or IP of the slave to be reported to the master during slave registration. Will appear in the output of SHOW SLAVE HOSTS. Leave unset if you do not want the slave to register itself with the master. Note that it is not sufficient for the master to simply read the IP of the slave off the socket once the slave connects. Due to NAT and other routing issues, that IP may not be valid for connecting to the slave from the master or other hosts

parameters.name: report_password
parameters.description: The account password of the slave to be reported to the master during slave registration

parameters.name: report_port
parameters.description: Port for connecting to slave reported to the master during slave registration. Set it only if the slave is listening on a non-default port or if you have a special tunnel from the master or other clients to the slave. If not sure, leave this option unset

parameters.name: report_user
parameters.description: The account user name of the slave to be reported to the master during slave registration

parameters.name: require_secure_transport
parameters.description: When this option is enabled, connections attempted using insecure transport will be rejected. Secure transports are SSL/TLS, Unix sockets or named pipes.

parameters.name: rowid_merge_buff_size
parameters.description: The size of the buffers used [NOT] IN evaluation via partial matching

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_master_enabled
parameters.description: Enable semi-synchronous replication master (disabled by default).

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_master_timeout
parameters.description: The timeout value (in ms) for semi-synchronous replication in the master

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_master_trace_level
parameters.description: The tracing level for semi-sync replication.

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_master_wait_no_slave
parameters.description: Wait until timeout when no semi-synchronous replication slave is available.

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_master_wait_point
parameters.description: Should transaction wait for semi-sync ack after having synced binlog, or after having committed in storage engine.

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_slave_delay_master
parameters.description: Only write master info file when ack is needed.

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_slave_enabled
parameters.description: Enable semi-synchronous replication slave (disabled by default).

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_slave_kill_conn_timeout
parameters.description: Timeout for the mysql connection used to kill the slave io_thread's connection on master. This timeout comes into play when stop slave is executed.

parameters.name: rpl_semi_sync_slave_trace_level
parameters.description: The tracing level for semi-sync replication.

parameters.name: secure_auth
parameters.description: Disallow authentication for accounts that have old (pre-4.1) passwords

parameters.name: secure_file_priv
parameters.description: Limit LOAD DATA, SELECT ... OUTFILE, and LOAD_FILE() to files within specified directory. Empty value means no limits except /proc

parameters.name: secure_timestamp
parameters.description: Restricts direct setting of a session timestamp. Possible levels are: YES - timestamp cannot deviate from the system clock, REPLICATION - replication thread can adjust timestamp to match the master's, SUPER - a user with this privilege and a replication thread can adjust timestamp, NO - historical behavior, anyone can modify session timestamp

parameters.name: server_id
parameters.description: Uniquely identifies the server instance in the community of replication partners

parameters.name: server_uid
parameters.description: Automatically calculated server unique id hash

parameters.name: session_track_schema
parameters.description: Track changes to the default schema.

parameters.name: session_track_state_change
parameters.description: Track changes to the session state.

parameters.name: session_track_system_variables
parameters.description: Track changes in registered system variables.

parameters.name: session_track_transaction_info
parameters.description: Track changes to the transaction attributes. OFF to disable; STATE to track just transaction state (Is there an active transaction? Does it have any data? etc.); CHARACTERISTICS to track transaction state and report all statements needed to start a transaction with the same characteristics (isolation level, read only/read write,snapshot - but not any work done / data modified within the transaction).

parameters.name: skip_external_locking
parameters.description: Don't use system (external) locking

parameters.name: skip_grant_tables
parameters.description: Start without grant tables. This gives all users FULL ACCESS to all tables.

parameters.name: skip_name_resolve
parameters.description: Don't resolve hostnames. All hostnames are IP's or 'localhost'.

parameters.name: skip_networking
parameters.description: Don't allow connection with TCP/IP

parameters.name: skip_show_database
parameters.description: Don't allow 'SHOW DATABASE' commands

parameters.name: slave_compressed_protocol
parameters.description: Use compression on master/slave protocol

parameters.name: slave_connections_needed_for_purge
parameters.description: Minimum number of connected slaves required for automatic binary log purge with max_binlog_total_size, binlog_expire_logs_seconds or binlog_expire_logs_days. Default is 0 when Galera is enabled and 1 otherwise.

parameters.name: slave_ddl_exec_mode
parameters.description: How replication events should be executed. Legal values are STRICT and IDEMPOTENT (default). In IDEMPOTENT mode, replication will not stop for DDL operations that are idempotent. This means that CREATE TABLE is treated as CREATE TABLE OR REPLACE and DROP TABLE is treated as DROP TABLE IF EXISTS.

parameters.name: slave_domain_parallel_threads
parameters.description: Maximum number of parallel threads to use on slave for events in a single replication domain. When using multiple domains, this can be used to limit a single domain from grabbing all threads and thus stalling other domains. The default of 0 means to allow a domain to grab as many threads as it wants, up to the value of slave_parallel_threads.

parameters.name: slave_exec_mode
parameters.description: How replication events should be executed. Legal values are STRICT (default) and IDEMPOTENT. In IDEMPOTENT mode, replication will not stop for operations that are idempotent. For example, in row based replication attempts to delete rows that doesn't exist will be ignored. In STRICT mode, replication will stop on any unexpected difference between the master and the slave.

parameters.name: slave_load_tmpdir
parameters.description: The location where the slave should put its temporary files when replicating a LOAD DATA INFILE command

parameters.name: slave_max_allowed_packet
parameters.description: The maximum packet length to sent successfully from the master to slave.

parameters.name: slave_max_statement_time
parameters.description: A query that has taken more than slave_max_statement_time seconds to run on the slave will be aborted. The argument will be treated as a decimal value with microsecond precision. A value of 0 (default) means no timeout

parameters.name: slave_net_timeout
parameters.description: Number of seconds to wait for more data from any master/slave connection before aborting the read

parameters.name: slave_parallel_max_queued
parameters.description: Limit on how much memory SQL threads should use per parallel replication thread when reading ahead in the relay log looking for opportunities for parallel replication. Only used when --slave-parallel-threads > 0.

parameters.name: slave_parallel_mode
parameters.description: Controls what transactions are applied in parallel when using --slave-parallel-threads. Possible values: "optimistic" tries to apply most transactional DML in parallel, and handles any conflicts with rollback and retry. "conservative" limits parallelism in an effort to avoid any conflicts. "aggressive" tries to maximise the parallelism, possibly at the cost of increased conflict rate. "minimal" only parallelizes the commit steps of transactions. "none" disables parallel apply completely.

parameters.name: slave_parallel_threads
parameters.description: If non-zero, number of threads to spawn to apply in parallel events on the slave that were group-committed on the master or were logged with GTID in different replication domains. Note that these threads are in addition to the IO and SQL threads, which are always created by a replication slave

parameters.name: slave_parallel_workers
parameters.description: Alias for slave_parallel_threads

parameters.name: slave_run_triggers_for_rbr
parameters.description: Modes for how triggers in row-base replication on slave side will be executed. Legal values are NO (default), YES, LOGGING and ENFORCE. NO means that trigger for RBR will not be running on slave. YES and LOGGING means that triggers will be running on slave, if there was not triggers running on the master for the statement. LOGGING also means results of that the executed triggers work will be written to the binlog. ENFORCE means that triggers will always be run on the slave, even if there are triggers on the master. ENFORCE implies LOGGING.

parameters.name: slave_skip_errors
parameters.description: Tells the slave thread to continue replication when a query event returns an error from the provided list

parameters.name: slave_sql_verify_checksum
parameters.description: Force checksum verification of replication events after reading them from relay log. Note: Events are always checksum-verified by slave on receiving them from the network before writing them to the relay log

parameters.name: slave_transaction_retries
parameters.description: Number of times the slave SQL thread will retry a transaction in case it failed with a deadlock, elapsed lock wait timeout or listed in slave_transaction_retry_errors, before giving up and stopping

parameters.name: slave_transaction_retry_errors
parameters.description: Tells the slave thread to retry transaction for replication when a query event returns an error from the provided list. Deadlock error, elapsed lock wait timeout, net read error, net read timeout, net write error, net write timeout, connect error and 2 types of lost connection error are automatically added to this list

parameters.name: slave_transaction_retry_interval
parameters.description: Interval of the slave SQL thread will retry a transaction in case it failed with a deadlock or elapsed lock wait timeout or listed in slave_transaction_retry_errors

parameters.name: slave_type_conversions
parameters.description: Set of slave type conversions that are enabled. If the variable is empty, no conversions are allowed and it is expected that the types match exactly

parameters.name: slow_launch_time
parameters.description: If creating the thread takes longer than this value (in seconds), the Slow_launch_threads counter will be incremented

parameters.name: slow_query_log
parameters.description: Alias for log_slow_query. Log slow queries to a table or log file. Defaults logging to a file 'hostname'-slow.log or a table mysql.slow_log if --log-output=TABLE is used. Must be enabled to activate other slow log options.

parameters.name: slow_query_log_file
parameters.description: Alias for log_slow_query_file. Log slow queries to given log file. Defaults logging to 'hostname'-slow.log. Must be enabled to activate other slow log options

parameters.name: socket
parameters.description: Socket file to use for connection

parameters.name: sort_buffer_size
parameters.description: Each thread that needs to do a sort allocates a buffer of this size

parameters.name: sql_auto_is_null
parameters.description: If set to 1, the query SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE auto_increment_column IS NULL will return an auto-increment that has just been successfully inserted, the same as the LAST_INSERT_ID() function. Some ODBC programs make use of this IS NULL comparison.

parameters.name: sql_big_selects
parameters.description: If set to 0, MariaDB will not perform large SELECTs. See max_join_size for details. If max_join_size is set to anything but DEFAULT, sql_big_selects is automatically set to 0. If sql_big_selects is again set, max_join_size will be ignored.

parameters.name: sql_buffer_result
parameters.description: If set to 1 (0 is default), results from SELECT statements are always placed into temporary tables. This can help the server when it takes a long time to send the results to the client by allowing the table locks to be freed early.

parameters.name: sql_if_exists
parameters.description: If set to 1 adds an implicate IF EXISTS to ALTER, RENAME and DROP of TABLES, VIEWS, FUNCTIONS and PACKAGES

parameters.name: sql_log_bin
parameters.description: If set to 0 (1 is the default), no logging to the binary log is done for the client. Only clients with the SUPER privilege can update this variable. Can have unintended consequences if set globally, see SET SQL_LOG_BIN. Starting MariaDB 10.1.7, this variable does not affect the replication of events in a Galera cluster.

parameters.name: sql_log_off
parameters.description: If set to 1 (0 is the default), no logging to the general query log is done for the client. Only clients with the SUPER privilege can update this variable.

parameters.name: sql_mode
parameters.description: Sets the sql mode

parameters.name: sql_notes
parameters.description: If set to 1, the default, warning_count is incremented each time a Note warning is encountered. If set to 0, Note warnings are not recorded. mysqldump has outputs to set this variable to 0 so that no unnecessary increments occur when data is reloaded. See also note_verbosity, which allows one to define with notes are sent.

parameters.name: sql_quote_show_create
parameters.description: If set to 1, the default, the server will quote identifiers for SHOW CREATE DATABASE, SHOW CREATE TABLE and SHOW CREATE VIEW statements. Quoting is disabled if set to 0. Enable to ensure replications works when identifiers require quoting.

parameters.name: sql_safe_updates
parameters.description: If set to 1, UPDATEs and DELETEs need either a key in the WHERE clause, or a LIMIT clause, or else they will aborted. Prevents the common mistake of accidentally deleting or updating every row in a table.

parameters.name: sql_select_limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows to return from SELECT statements

parameters.name: sql_slave_skip_counter

ON is required on a source before any replica can use SOURCE_AUTO_POSITION=1. To safely switch from OFF to ON, first set all servers to OFF_PERMISSIVE, then set all servers to ON_PERMISSIVE, then wait for all transactions without a GTID to be replicated and executed on all servers, and finally set all servers to GTID_MODE = ON.

parameters.name: log_error

parameters.name: log_error_services

parameters.name: log_error_suppression_list

parameters.name: log_throttle_queries_not_using_indexes

parameters.name: log_timestamps
parameters.description: UTC to timestamp log files in zulu time, for more concise timestamps and easier correlation of logs from servers from multiple time zones, or SYSTEM to use the system's local time. parameters.name: read_rnd_buffer_size
parameters.description: When reading rows in sorted order after a sort, the rows are read through this buffer to avoid a disk seeks

parameters.name: regexp_stack_limit
parameters.description: Stack size limit for regular expressions matches

parameters.name: regexp_time_limit
parameters.description: Timeout for regular expressions matches, in steps of the match engine, typically on the order of milliseconds.

parameters.name: relay_log
parameters.description: The location and name to use for relay logs

parameters.name: relay_log_index
parameters.description: File that holds the names for relay log files.

parameters.name: relay_log_info_file
parameters.description: The location and name of the file that remembers where the SQL replication thread is in the relay logs

parameters.name: relay_log_info_repository
parameters.description: Defines the type of the repository for the relay log information and associated workers.

parameters.name: relay_log_purge
parameters.description: if disabled - do not purge relay logs. if enabled - purge them as soon as they are no more needed (Defaults to on; use --skip-relay-log-purge to disable.)

parameters.name: relay_log_recovery
parameters.description: If enabled, existing relay logs will be skipped by the replication threads. The receiver will start a new relay log and the applier will start reading from the beginning of that file. The receiver's position relative to the source will be reset to the applier's position relative to the source; the receiver uses this in case SOURCE_AUTO_POSITION=0.

parameters.name: relay_log_space_limit
parameters.description: Maximum space to use for all relay logs

parameters.name: replica_allow_batching
parameters.description: Allow this replica to batch requests when using the NDB storage engine. (Defaults to on; use --skip-replica-allow-batching to disable.)

parameters.name: replica_checkpoint_group
parameters.description: When using multi-threaded applier (replica_parallel_workers>0), it will update the worker progress status periodically. This option specifies the maximum number of committed transactions between updates.

parameters.name: replica_checkpoint_period
parameters.description: When using a multi-threaded applier (replica_parallel_workers>0), it will update the worker progress status periodically. This option specifies the maximum number of milliseconds between updates.

parameters.name: replica_compressed_protocol
parameters.description: Use compression in the source/replica protocol.

parameters.name: replica_exec_mode
parameters.description: Modes for how replication events should be executed. Legal values are STRICT (default) and IDEMPOTENT. In IDEMPOTENT mode, replication will ignore duplicate key errors and key not found errors. In STRICT mode, replication will stop at those errors.

parameters.name: replica_load_tmpdir
parameters.description: The location where this replica will store temporary files when replicating a LOAD DATA INFILE command from a source having binlog_format=STATEMENT.

parameters.name: replica_max_allowed_packet
parameters.description: The maximum size of packets sent from an upstream source server to this server.

parameters.name: replica_net_timeout
parameters.description: Number of seconds to wait for more data from a replication connection before aborting the read.

parameters.name: replica_parallel_type
parameters.description: The method used by the replication applier to parallelize transactions. DATABASE, indicates that it may apply transactions in parallel in case they update different databases. LOGICAL_CLOCK, which is the default, indicates that it decides whether two transactions can be applied in parallel using the logical timestamps computed by the source, according to binlog_transaction_dependency_tracking.

parameters.name: replica_parallel_workers
parameters.description: Number of worker threads for executing events in parallel

parameters.name: replica_pending_jobs_size_max
parameters.description: Soft limit on the size, in bytes, of per-worker queues of events that have not yet been applied. The queue size may exceed this limit in case a single event is bigger than the limit.

parameters.name: replica_preserve_commit_order
parameters.description: Force replication worker threads to commit in the same order as on the source. Enabled by default (Defaults to on; use --skip-replica-preserve-commit-order to disable.)

parameters.name: replica_skip_errors
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of error numbers. If an applier thread on this replica encounters one of these errors while applying a Query_log_event, it will ignore the error, rather than stop.

parameters.name: replica_sql_verify_checksum
parameters.description: Force checksum verification of replication events after reading them from relay log. Note: The replica always verifies checksums for events received from the network, if the event has a checksum at all, before it writes the event to the relay log. Enabled by default. (Defaults to on; use --skip-replica-sql-verify-checksum to disable.)

parameters.name: replica_transaction_retries
parameters.description: Number of times the replication applier will retry a transaction in case it failed with a deadlock or other transient error, before it gives up and stops.

parameters.name: replica_type_conversions
parameters.description: Set of type conversions that may be used by the replication applier thread for row events. Allowed values are: ALL_LOSSY to enable lossy conversions, ALL_NON_LOSSY to enable non-lossy conversions, ALL_UNSIGNED to treat all integer column type data to be unsigned values, and ALL_SIGNED to treat all integer column type data to be signed values. Default treatment is ALL_SIGNED. If ALL_SIGNED and ALL_UNSIGNED both are specified, ALL_SIGNED will take higher priority than ALL_UNSIGNED. If the variable is assigned the empty set, no conversions are allowed and it is expected that the types match exactly.

parameters.name: replication_optimize_for_static_plugin_config
parameters.description: Optional flag that blocks plugin install/uninstall and allows skipping the acquisition of the lock to read from the plugin list and the usage of read-optimized spin-locks. Use only when plugin hook callback needs optimization (a lot of semi-sync replicas, for instance).

parameters.name: replication_sender_observe_commit_only
parameters.description: Optional flag that allows for only calling back observer hooks at commit.

parameters.name: report_host
parameters.description: Hostname or IP that this replica will report to the source while initiating the replication connection. Will appear in the output of SHOW REPLICAS. Leave this unset if you do not want the replica to register itself with the source. Note that it is not sufficient for the source to simply read the IP of the replica off the socket once the replica connects: in the presence of NAT other routing features, that IP may not be valid for connecting to the replica from the source or other hosts.

parameters.name: report_password
parameters.description: The account password that this replica will report to the source while initiating the replication connection.

parameters.name: report_port
parameters.description: The port for connecting to the replica, which this replica will report to the source while initiating the replication connection. Set it only if the replica is listening on a non-default port or if you have a special tunnel from the source or other clients to this replica. If not sure, leave this option unset.

parameters.name: report_user
parameters.description: The account user name that this replica will report to the source while initiating the replication connection.

parameters.name: require_secure_transport
parameters.description: When this option is enabled, connections attempted using insecure transport will be rejected.  Secure transports are SSL/TLS, Unix socket or Shared Memory (on Windows).

parameters.name: rpl_read_size
parameters.description: The size for reads done from the binlog and relay log. It must be a multiple of 4kb. Making it larger might help with IO stalls while reading these files when they are not in the OS buffer cache

parameters.name: rpl_stop_replica_timeout
parameters.description: Timeout in seconds to wait for replication threads to stop, before STOP REPLICA returns a warning.

parameters.name: rpl_stop_slave_timeout

parameters.name: schema_definition_cache

parameters.name: secure_file_priv

parameters.name: select_into_buffer_size

parameters.name: select_into_disk_sync
parameters.description: Synchronize flushed buffer with disk for SELECT INTO OUTFILE/DUMPFILE.

parameters.name: select_into_disk_sync_delay
parameters.description: The delay in milliseconds after each buffer sync for SELECT INTO OUTFILE/DUMPFILE. Requires select_into_sync_disk = ON.

parameters.name: sha256_password_auto_generate_rsa_keys
